newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Bekaert first half profit fell 25 percent.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Bekaert first half profit fell 25 percent.

text.p: Belgian steel wire and cord maker Bekaert NV reported on Wednesday a 25 percent drop in group net profit for the first six months of 1996 but said full year earnings would rise thanks to the sale of shares in Japanese subsidiary Bridgestone Metalpha Corp (BMA).

Bekaert said a worse-than-expected slump in demand for its products in Europe squeezed margins in the first half, leaving group net profit for the period at 1.27 billion Belgian francs ($40.72 million).

"Consolidated profit for the full year 1996 will be substantially higher than in 1995 due to a capital gain of 2.2 billion Belgian francs on the sale of 10.1 million BMA shares sold in July," Bekaert said in a statement.
Sales rose three percent to 32.94 billion francs, but on a comparable basis, excluding recent acquisitions, slipped nearly four percent.
"For the current operations Bekaert does not expect any significant improvement in profitability for the second half of the year," the company said.
Bekaert said in July it expected current earnings to be about 15 percent down on 1995's 3.0 billion Belgian francs. ($1=31.19 Belgian Franc)
